enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
535 PM MDT Sun Oct 25 2026

...New AVIATION...


.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 527 PM MDT Sun Oct 25 2026

 - Storm chances shift east on Sunday and Monday, limited mostly
   to Hudspeth and Otero Counties. A few storms will be capable of
   large hail, gusty winds, and excessive rainfall leading to 
   localized flash flooding.
   

 - A few days of drier weather is expected midweek before rain 
   chances return Thursday into next weekend.

 - Typical late-October temperatures, with lowland highs in the
   lower to mid 70s.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1112 AM MDT Sun Oct 25 2026

The weather pattern will be somewhat less active this afternoon 
and evening as the large low pressure system near the Four Corners
Region lifts out of the area to the east. the Sub-tropical jet 
remains near the area and will continue to help generate isolated
to scattered thunderstorm development over areas east of the Rio
Grande late this afternoon and overnight. The most likely areas of
storm development will be in Otero, Hudspeth, El Paso Counties 
and locations to the east. There will be a few isolated 
thunderstorms in the afternoon, but the most active period will be
later in the evening after 9 pm when a short wave trough embedded
in the flow pattern helps generate scattered strong thunderstorm 
development. The severe threat from storms will be reduced but 
still possible. There is a potential for excessive rainfall with 
flash flooding from a few storms, but should not be as widespread 
as previous days. 

Monday should be a quieter day as the local forecast area will be
west of the trough axis with a drier, more stable mass moving into
the region. Short range models seem to reflect this with only a
few brief isolated storms for areas east of El Paso in the evening
hours. Tuesday and Wednesday will be dry for southern New Mexico
and Far West Texas as a dry westerly zonal flow sets up over the
region. Temperatures will be near seasonal in most areas. 

We will return to a more active weather pattern Thursday and
Friday as another trough sets up on the west coast and a ridge
builds over the Gulf Coast. This pattern will allow moisture back
into the region that will help fuel scattered showers and
thunderstorms across the area both days. 

The outlook for Halloween on Saturday looks dry with a short wave
ridge moving over the state for a short period of quiet weather.
Active weather returns to the area next Sunday as the trough on
the west coast deepens and moves inland toward New Mexico.  

&&

.AVIATION...
(00Z TAFS)
Issued at 527 PM MDT Sun Oct 25 2026

A lot less thunderstorms this evening than the last couple of
days. Having said that, there are currently a few isolated storms
in the Tularosa Basin and the latest convective allowing models
have more thunderstorms developing around 9 PM, mainly for
locations east of the Rio Grande. Winds away from the
thunderstorms will be light tonight and those less than 10 knot
winds will continue on Monday. We have some mid and high ceilings
this early evening, but later tonight we will still have some
clouds, but our ceilings will be unlimited. On Monday we will
again see a slight chance for thunderstorms mainly east of KELP.
We could see some high ceilings of BKN250 for parts of the day on
Monday.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1112 AM MDT Sun Oct 25 2026

Dry conditions for Gila NF, but scattered thunderstorms are
expected again across Lincoln NF this afternoon and evening. 
Storms will be capable of gusty winds and localized flooding. 
Prevailing wind out of the SSW at 5 to 10 mph, with Good vent 
rates today. Lighter winds Monday/Tuesday will keep vent rates 
Poor to Fair through most of the afternoon hours. 

Moisture shifts further east early this week, leading to a brief 
window of dry conditions area wide. Rain chances return Thursday 
into next weekend, leading to another round of wetting 
precipitation over the forested areas. ERCs are very low at the 
moment, so no fire danger expected into early November.

&&
